evaluations.rationale: Faithful nursery-rhyme spine with essentially all source beats retained in order and theme intact; naming ELI/CLARA and giving Teacher/Eli short unquoted lines is light closed-cast connective tissue, not major invented plot, so fidelity stays high rather than severe-penalty territory. Cast locks are excellent and restated on re-entry (Mary’s braids/blue pinafore/bonnet; lamb’s snowy fleece/red ribbon; Teacher’s gray dress/white collar; distinct pupil looks). Action is almost entirely single-clip observable micro-beats with proper grounding after every heading, ideal for 5–10s AI clips. Pacing is slightly over-fragmented: two consecutive EXT. SCHOOLHOUSE YARD - AFTERNOON headings and a near-reprise lane beat pad a very short source. Dialogue VO tracks the verse well, but invented pupil banter and Teacher’s ejection line exceed the summarized-exchange cap. Sound/music parentheticals are concrete, present in every scene, and escalate appropriately at the reunion and moral close. Medium lock and vision sidecar are correct for a children’s rhyme. No deal-breakers.
evaluations.promptImprovementSuggestion: Tighten the summarized-exchange rule: when the source attributes speech or a reaction to an unnamed group without quoting individuals, allow at most one named supporting token a single book-close line and put all other group reaction in Action only—forbid distributing invented banter across multiple newly named speakers.

judgeSummaryNotes: Strongest: Screenplay A because it is the sole candidate and delivers a clip-ready, medium-locked picture-book adaptation with consistent cast looks, full diegetic sound beds, and near-complete verse coverage. Weakest: Screenplay A because minor invented pupil/teacher dialogue and a duplicated afternoon schoolyard heading are the clearest fixable drains on book-only speech discipline and scene economy.
